description: Golden Q&A pairs for the Blackbox RAG pipeline. 'expectedSources' are knowledge_chunks.source_id values (a trailing '#' matches any section of a note). 'answerable: false' items must be declined.

items.question: How should I evaluate a RAG pipeline?
items.referenceAnswer: Evaluate retrieval separately from generation: build a golden set and measure recall@k and MRR, then measure answer faithfulness, answer relevance and citation accuracy, and re-run on every change to chunking, embeddings or prompts.

items.question: Why combine keyword search with vector search in retrieval?
items.referenceAnswer: Dense vectors capture meaning but miss exact identifiers, error codes and rare terms; keyword search catches those. Combining both and fusing rankings, for example with reciprocal rank fusion, improves recall.

items.question: When should I optimise for precision rather than recall?
items.referenceAnswer: Optimise for precision when false positives are costly, such as spam filtering; optimise for recall when missing positives is costly, such as fraud or disease screening. Choose the decision threshold from the business cost of each error.

items.question: My model does well on training data but badly on validation data. What should I do?
items.referenceAnswer: That is high variance (overfitting). Add data, regularise with L2, dropout or early stopping, or simplify the model, and check for leakage and use learning curves to confirm.

items.question: How do I detect data drift for a model in production?
items.referenceAnswer: Monitor input feature distributions and prediction distributions against a reference window with statistical tests, track model quality when labels arrive, alert on sustained shifts and define a retraining trigger.

items.question: Explain the trade-off between consistency and availability in distributed systems.
items.referenceAnswer: During a network partition a distributed store must choose between consistency and availability. Strong consistency suits balances and inventory; eventual consistency suits feeds and counters.

items.question: How do I make a payment API safe to retry?
items.referenceAnswer: Use idempotency keys so a retried request with the same key returns the original result instead of charging twice, store the key with the outcome, and make handlers idempotent.

items.question: How should I structure an answer to a behavioral question?
items.referenceAnswer: Use STAR: a short situation, your task, the actions you took with your reasoning in first person, and a measurable result plus what you learned. Spend most of the time on the action.

items.question: How do I get into a group discussion that is already busy?
items.referenceAnswer: Wait for a natural pause, acknowledge the previous speaker by name, and add one new idea with an example or a number rather than repeating what was said.

items.question: What makes a good summary at the end of a group discussion?
items.referenceAnswer: A neutral, short summary of the main arguments on each side and where the group converged, without adding new points or declaring a winner.

items.question: What should I say in an interview when I don't know the answer?
items.referenceAnswer: Say so honestly, then reason from what you do know, ask a clarifying question, state assumptions and work toward a partial answer.

items.question: What is the KV cache in transformer inference?
items.referenceAnswer: During autoregressive decoding the keys and values of earlier tokens are cached so each new token only computes attention for itself, trading memory for much faster generation.
